articles.title: Annuity vs Equal Principal: Building Both Amortization Schedules in TypeScript
articles.excerpt: Two loans can have the same principal, rate, and term while producing very different monthly bills. The difference is often the amortization method: Annuity (also called a fixed-payment or level-payme…
articles.body: Two loans can have the same principal, rate, and term while producing very different monthly bills. The difference is often the amortization method: Annuity (also called a fixed-payment or level-payment schedule) keeps the total scheduled payment constant when the rate is fixed. Equal principal pays the same amount of principal every month, so the total payment starts higher and falls over time. Neither method is a mysterious financial product. Both follow the same monthly loop: calculate interest from the opening balance, decide how much principal is paid, reduce the balance, and record the row. The implementation choice is about the rule that determines the principal portion.

articles.title: Adding a second language to a static Next.js site without changing a single URL
articles.excerpt: My small quiz site started English-only: a Next.js App Router project, output: 'export', deployed as static files. When I added a French version, I had three rules: No English URL could change. They w…
articles.body: My small quiz site started English-only: a Next.js App Router project, output: 'export' , deployed as static files. When I added a French version, I had three rules: No English URL could change. They were already indexed. Each page had to declare its real language in <html lang> . No i18n middleware — a static export has no server to run it. Here's the setup that satisfied all three, plus the one gotcha that cost me an afternoon. Why a subdirectory, not a subdomain /fr rather than fr.example.com or a separate domain. A subdirectory shares the domain's existing authority, so the French pages didn't start from zero in search. That turned out to matter: a few days after launch, the French pages were getting impressions faster than the English ones had.

articles.title: How one user's StatefulSet edit could land a pod in someone else's namespace
articles.excerpt: How one user's StatefulSet edit could land a pod in someone else's namespace On September 23, Kubernetes shipped fixes for CVE-2026-2270, a confused deputy bug in the StatefulSet controller. The short…
articles.body: How one user's StatefulSet edit could land a pod in someone else's namespace On September 23, Kubernetes shipped fixes for CVE-2026-2270, a confused deputy bug in the StatefulSet controller. The short version: a user with write access to StatefulSets and ControllerRevisions in one namespace could get the cluster itself to create a pod in a different namespace. The cluster did the crossing. The user just pointed. If you run a shared cluster, this one is worth understanding, because the pattern behind it shows up everywhere. The wall everyone trusts Namespaces are the walls of Kubernetes. You give team A their own namespace, team B theirs, and RBAC rules make sure nobody reaches across. A user who can only touch team-a should never be able to create anything in team-b .

articles.body: Building a Web App: A Beginner's Guide to Cloud Architecture (Part 5 of 5) In Part 1, our main server died, but our load balancer instantly shifted traffic to a backup (High Availability). In Part 2, 50,000 users rushed our registration page, and our infrastructure automatically cloned itself to handle the massive spike (Scalability). In Part 3, malicious actors tried to bypass our website, but our private networks and firewalls blocked them (Security). In Part 4, international users complained about lag, so we moved our static files to global edge networks to make the app lightning fast (Speed). articles.title: Getting an old HP LaserJet P1102 to print on macOS 27
articles.excerpt: I plugged my HP LaserJet P1102 into my Mac and printed a page. macOS said the job was done. Nothing came out. No error, no paper jam, nothing. HP has no driver for this printer on current macOS. Here…
articles.body: I plugged my HP LaserJet P1102 into my Mac and printed a page. macOS said the job was done. Nothing came out. No error, no paper jam, nothing. HP has no driver for this printer on current macOS. Here is what was wrong and how I got it to print. The cause Two separate problems, and the first one hides the second. macOS picked the wrong driver. When it can't find the right one, it falls back to "HP LaserJet Series PCL 4/5". The P1102 can't use it. It is a host-based printer: the Mac has to render the page in HP's own format, and the printer can't read the standard PCL language at all. It receives the job and drops it silently. The right driver refuses to install. HP's last Mac driver for this printer is Apple's "HP Printer Drivers 5.1.1" from 2021.

articles.body: Two months after the bombshell news that a swarm of its agents had broken their containment and hacked into the computers of the AI company Hugging Face , OpenAI is still putting out fires. A steady drip of disclosures about other hacks in the weeks since has kept OpenAI in the spotlight and raised serious questions about the safety of its technology. Last week brought news of another hack, this time into Australia’s national health-care system. The Australian government says that OpenAI did not notify it of the breach until 84 days after it happened. But OpenAI insists it is not on the back foot.

articles.title: NASA Opens 2027 Human Lander Challenge for Lunar Communications
articles.excerpt: NASA’s 2027 Human Lander Challenge is seeking ideas from college and university students to help address one of the most critical needs for sustained lunar exploration: reliable communications. As NAS…
articles.body: 3 Min Read NASA Opens 2027 Human Lander Challenge for Lunar Communications NASA’s 2027 Human Lander Challenge is seeking ideas from college and university students to help address one of the most critical needs for sustained lunar exploration: reliable communications. As NASA prepares for long-term human presence on the Moon through the Artemis and Moon Base programs, communications systems will be just as important as spacecraft and rockets. A resilient communications system will connect astronauts, rovers, habitats, landers, mission support teams on Earth, and more. Reliable communications are essential for ensuring safety, coordinating complex operations, and enabling timely decision-making in the harsh and remote lunar environment.

articles.body: NASA has awarded a contract to Omitron Inc. for the acquisition of orbital safety analysis services, which provide for critical protection of NASA spaceflight assets and astronaut lives. This indefinite-delivery contract is valued at approximately $23.5 million over a five-year period of performance and entails conjunction assessment screening services for all NASA uncrewed spacecraft, support of human spaceflight activities, and orbital safety analysis support to the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration’s Office of Space Commerce.

articles.body: TL;DR OpenAI is introducing GPT-6.1 Sol, promising Astra-like performance at one-fifth the expenditure. Across numerous benchmarks, GPT-6.1 Sol comes close to 6 Astra’s capabilities, and outpaces GPT-6 Sol. GPT-6.1 demonstrates fewer factual errors than GPT-6 Sol across similar tests. DevDay is here for OpenAI, and that means the company is sharing a whole bunch of news about its latest work on models and the services built around them. While we just heard that GPT-6.1 Astra is getting sent back to the bench for misbehaving, progress continues on the rest of OpenAI’s headlining models, and this afternoon we’re getting the scoop on the first member of that 6.1-series to actually make its public debut, with the launch of GPT‑6.1 Sol.
